ABSTRACT

The paper investigates adaptive automated control algorithms for a corona discharge – based plasma-chemical water disinfection system. The study analyzes operating conditions with pulsed voltage in the range of 5-30 kV, pulse repetition frequency of 1-20 kHz, duty cycle of 0,2-0,7, water electrical conductivity of 100-1200 μS/cm, and temperature of 15-30 °C. The results show that a 10-15% deviation in pulsed voltage increases discharge current instability by 8-18% and leads to a 10-25% rise in energy consumption.The application of the proposed control algorithm reduces voltage and current fluctuations by 20-35% and decreases energy consumption by 15-30%, while maintaining a stable microbiological inactivation level of 3-5 log. These findings confirm the effectiveness of the adaptive control approach for corona discharge – based plasma-chemical water disinfection systems.
